analysis: Examined three files. (1) EngineV2Bridge+Translation.swift: the only change is a new constant `unsupportedOutputControlPrefix` (head lines 251-254). It is unused in the supplied text, with no behavior change. The existing cacheScope-to-cacheSalt mapping (lines 78-82) is unchanged, so T-041 salt scoping is intact. (2) EngineV2RequestUsageSignal.swift: `_firstWithheldReasoningAt` is renamed to `_firstWithheldOutputAt`, and a new `recordWithheldOutput()` is added (head lines 251-255). It stores only a timestamp under the lock and no plaintext. `_withheldReasoning` remains request-local plaintext that is never logged. Callers of the old `firstWithheldReasoningAt` name are outside the supplied evidence; a missed rename would be a compile error rather than a security issue. (3) MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (patch only, truncated excerpt): GLM JSON response_format and forced tool calls are now withheld until validated. `emit()` yields events only when there is no glmAnswer, or the validated visible portion; `validatedAnswer` is yielded after `formatOutput.validate`. Fail-closed paths call `releaseBox.fire()` and `finish(throwing:)`. GLM media combined with withholding output is rejected up front with invalidToolPayload and the release box fired. The privacy-relevant timing signal is only the interval recorded locally. Nothing is logged or sent beyond existing paths. Remaining integration questions, not findings: the implementations of GLM5NextPromptPolicy.withholdsOutput, GLM5NextResponseFormatOutput.withholding/validatedAnswer and prepared.glmResponseFormat are not supplied, so the exact no-leak guarantee of withheld text is unverified. The pre-existing nativeReasoningPrefix gating now also applies to GLM. The consumer of firstWithheldOutputAt (TTFT or usage metrics) is not shown, so I cannot confirm the answer-only timestamp doesn't change billing or telemetry semantics. No regression against T-008, T-041, T-053 or the TB-002 and TB-007 assumptions was identified from the supplied evidence.
